title: Federal and government cloud editions: FedRAMP, DoD IL5 and other certifications as marketed

prose.text: {{fed-products}} Government host names and identity hosts are in [[shared.oneapi.government-clouds]]; the cloud names are in [[shared.cloud-architecture.cloud-names]].

Whether the government cloud has dedicated infrastructure apart from the commercial cloud is open {{gap:fed-dedicated}}. Whether new features reach it later is open {{gap:fed-features}}, and where its data is stored is open {{gap:fed-residency}}.

Federal adoption figures are open {{gap:fed-adoption}}. Whether the government editions are variants of each product is open {{gap:fed-editions}}. Whether zscalerten and ZPA GOV or GOVUS are government cloud names is open {{gap:fed-names}}. The innovations document the legacy doc cites is not captured {{gap:fed-govcloud-capture}}.

checks.do: For a question about certifications, answer as the page markets them and name the authorization level and product scope the page gives.

fed-zia-high.statement: The public-sector page calls ZIA the only SASE Trusted Internet Connections (TIC) 3.0 solution with FedRAMP High authorization.

quotes: the only secure access service edge (SASE) Trusted Internet Connections (TIC) 3.0 solution with FedRAMP High authorization

fed-jab.statement: The page says ZIA and ZPA maintain JAB-High authorization.

quotes: Both ZIA and ZPA products maintain JAB-High authorization.

fed-moderate.statement: The page says ZIA and ZPA have held FedRAMP Moderate authorization since 2018.

quotes: FedRAMP Moderate**: ZIA and ZPA authorized since 2018

fed-il5.statement: The page says ZPA holds DoD IL5 (Impact Level 5) authorization.

quotes: DoD IL5 (Impact Level 5) authorization for ZPA

fed-certs.statement: The page lists CMMC Level 2 certification, GovRAMP authorization, CJIS Security Policy compliance, and FIPS 140-2, ISO 27001 and NIST 800-53 standards.

fed-products.statement: The page lists ZIA, ZPA and ZDX among its government-specific products.

fed-govcloud-capture.title: The government cloud innovations document
fed-govcloud-capture.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Captures: zscaler-government-public-sector-marketing.md, zscaler-govcloud-innovations.md.' The legacy doc cites zscaler-govcloud-innovations.md, which is not captured under vendor/zscaler-help/, so statements that rest on it cannot be cited.

fed-dedicated.title: Whether government cloud infrastructure is dedicated
fed-dedicated.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'GovCloud has dedicated infrastructure separate from commercial — not just a logical partition.' No captured page says this.

fed-features.title: Whether features reach the government cloud later than commercial
fed-features.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Feature availability: newer features may launch in commercial cloud first, gov second; some commercial features are restricted in gov.' No captured page says this.

fed-residency.title: Where government cloud data is stored
fed-residency.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Data residency: gov-cloud data stays in-region (US).' No captured page says this.

fed-adoption.title: Federal adoption figures
fed-adoption.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Adoption: 1M+ federal users; 13 of 15 cabinet agencies.' The public-sector capture names customers (FCC, State of Oklahoma, MCNC) but no such counts.

fed-editions.title: Whether government editions are variants of each product
fed-editions.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Regulated-cloud editions of the existing product line ... ZIA / ZPA / ZCC etc. all have gov-cloud variants ... not strictly separate products.' The public-sector capture lists government products for ZIA, ZPA and ZDX only and does not mention ZCC or editions.

fed-names.title: Government cloud names beyond the captured hosts
fed-names.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Federal Cloud variants (zscalergov, zscalerten, ZPA GOV / GOVUS).' The captured OneAPI guide and SDK routing name zscalergov hosts; no captured page names zscalerten or ZPA GOV / GOVUS.
